steps.title: Build the twin, and tonight's problem
steps.say: Sixteen signalised intersections in an invented city. A stadium in the north-east corner empties from minute 10, and the main road away from it has a lane shut. Today every signal runs the same 90-second cycle with equal greens.

body.name: Stadium event with a lane closure

steps.title: What is on the road right now?
steps.say: Detectors miscount by a few percent and a tenth of queue readings never arrive. Thirty minutes of detector data are fed in, and a filter on each link combines counts with readings into an estimated queue, with a margin.

steps.title: The evening with today's timing
steps.say: The whole hour is simulated in five-second steps under the plan in the field: vehicles queue, are released on green if there is room ahead, and back up into the intersection behind when there is not.

steps.title: Search for a better plan
steps.say: The optimiser tries three cycle lengths and hundreds of small changes to greens and offsets, keeping only changes that help and never a plan that breaks a safety rule. The result is then tested on five evenings of demand it never saw, beside the plan in the field and a simpler method.

steps.title: Two things the system refuses
steps.say: A hand-made plan that gives cars a long green by leaving pedestrians eight seconds to cross is refused, with the rule it breaks. And the analyst who asked for the optimised plan cannot approve it.

steps.title: An engineer approves, and nothing is deployed
steps.say: A traffic engineer reviews the evidence and approves. Approval produces a versioned plan for each intersection to export. This system has no connection to any signal controller.

body.note: Reviewed against the event plan; minimum greens and offsets checked.

steps.title: The audit trail
steps.say: Who created the scenario, who proposed the plan, who approved it and why: recorded in a log that cannot be edited.
